paragraphs: Bintilat yadayim tzarik sheyyitkavven hannotel lintila hammaksheret laakila, velaken en notelin miqqop velo miqqatan pachot mishshesh sheen lo machshaba vekavvana, zot veod acheret "p shennatal kaddin vekivven lintila hammaksheret im kol zeh tzarik hu lishmor tahorat yadayv bemachshabto vekavvanato, sheim hissicha dato mishshemirat yadayv zeman merubbeh "p sheeno yodea shennageu yadayv bimqomot metunnapim im kol zeh tzarik lachazor velittol, beopen shetztzarik lihyot mesim dato vekavvanato al tahorat yadayv kol meshek seuddato, vehaynu mippene deiqqar gerush hassitra achara hayeta al yede kavvanato, ulekak rauy shello yassicha dato mittahora zo kol zeman sheokel, velazeh amar hakkatub (qohelet t, z) "lek ekol besimcha lachmeka ushateh beleb tob yeneka ki kebar ratza haelohim et maaseka", vehaynu besimcha otiyyot machshaba veamar al yede hammachashaba v"y leb tob shehu hakkavvana ratza haelohim et maaseka, ki maaseh lebaddah bilti tzerup kavvana umachshaba enah ola leratzon, venaqet shem elohim al derek shekkatabti leel ki meqom hammachashaba vehakkavvana hu mocha veleb shemmisparam mispar elohim, velaken gam hattora shennimshela laakila ushetiyya diktib (mishle t, h) "leku lachamu belachami ushetu beyayin masaketti" gam ken hessach haddaat mazziq behah dilkak tzivva hashshem yitbarak (debarim d, t) raq hishshamer leka ushemor napsheka meod pen tishkach et haddebarim asher rau eneka upen yasuru millebabeka kol yeme chayyeka, veameru pen tishkach qae al hammocha sheshsham hashshikcha bar minnan:

clarification.explanation: In washing the hands, the one washing must intend a washing that qualifies him for eating; therefore one does not wash the hands of someone who lacks the capacity to intend it (a monkey, or a minor under the age of six). And even if he washed properly and had the right intention, he must guard the purity of his hands in his thought throughout the entire meal — and if he let his mind wander from this for a long time, he must go back and wash again, even though he does not know for certain that his hands touched a soiled place, since the essential expulsion of impurity is accomplished through the intention; therefore it is forbidden to let one's mind wander from this purity for as long as one is eating. On this the Ben Ish Chai brings an allusion from the verse, "Go, eat your bread with joy... and drink your wine with a good heart, for God has already accepted your deeds": the word "besimchah" (with joy) has the same letters as "machshavah" (thought), and "a good heart" is the intention — and it is only through the joining of thought (in the brain) and intention (in the heart) that "God has accepted your deeds," for a deed alone, without intention and thought, does not rise to be accepted (and the name "Elohim" is alluded to here because the brain and heart, the seat of thought and intention, have the same numerical value as the name Elohim). The same applies to Torah study, which is compared to eating and drinking ("Come, eat of my bread and drink of the wine I have mixed") — there too, a wandering mind is harmful, which is why we were warned, "Only take heed to yourself and guard your soul diligently, lest you forget the things your eyes have seen... all the days of your life," for "lest you forget" corresponds to the brain, the seat of forgetfulness.
takeaways: The washing requires the intention of the one washing (not that of a monkey or minor), and one must maintain the intention for purity throughout the entire meal, not only at the moment of washing.

The verse "with joy... and with a good heart" alludes together to thought (in the brain) and intention (in the heart) — "besimchah" has the letters of "machshavah"; and likewise in Torah study a wandering mind is harmful, and "lest you forget" corresponds to the brain.

paragraphs: Keshem shehessach haddaat meakkeb baakila ushetiyya leinyan beraka, ken shinnuy maqom meakkeb leinyan beraka, umeachar derabbu haddeot bazeh veanu qayma lan sapeq berakot lehaqel apillu neged maran za"l sheqqibbalnu horaotayv, laken nazkir pesaq hahalaka mah sheheelu haacharonim latzet yede choba hakkelal shel sapeq berakot lehaqel, vehu sheim saad bemaqom acher shebberak hammotzi veakal pat, ubetok seuddato shinna meqomo apillu shehalak lebayit acher vaapillu lo hinnicha shum adam bashshulchan, im hissicha dato milleekol az yebarek al debarim sheenam mechamat hasseuda im yirtzeh leekol, ben sheokelam babbayit hashsheni ben sheokelam bimqomo harishon leachar shechazar elayv aach"k, abal debarim shehem baim mechamat hasseuda lo yebarek alehem ben babbayit hashsheni ben keshechazar limqomo babbayit harishon v"p shehissicha dato, mippene dekol shehu betok seuddato la chashib gemar seuda yaan dehappat tzarik sheyyebarek alayv birkat hammazon bimqomo, lepikak keshehu omed mimmeqomo lelek lemaqom acher en amidato gemar seuddato, "p shehissicha dato milleekol shehare tzarik hu lachazor limqomo lebarek birkat hammazon, ulekak kaasher chozer veokel debarim shehem baim mechamat hasseuda al daat seuddato harishona hu asa kede lesayyem seuddato, ulekak en lebarek alehem battechilla, vekol shekken keshechozer veokel bimqomo harishon shehu meqom seuddato sheen lebarek techilla:

Vekol zeh ayre beabar veshinna meqomo, abal lekattechilla tzarik lizzaher shello laaqor misseuddato veligmor otah bemaqom acher ad sheyyebarek birkat hammazon, apillu im hinnicha miqtzat chaberim al hashshulchan, yaan dekol dabar hattaun leacharayv beraka bimqomo mippene chashibuto, tzarik lebarek acharayv qodem sheyyeaqer mimmeqomo, ki kemo shemmoelet chashibuto shello lebarek bemaqom acher, kak moelet chashibuto ledabar zeh shave lebarek qodem sheyyeaqer v"p shehu okel gam ken bammaqom hashsheni umebarek sham denimtza gam ken mebarek birkat hammazon bimqom akila, im kol zeh mah moil bekak laakila harishona shehayeta teuna beraka bimqomah lekattechilla qodem sheyyaaqor mishsham mishshum chashibut, ella sheim kebar aqar en tzarik lachazor ulebarek techilla al mah sheokel bammaqom hashsheni, shebbazeh lo yetaqqen et asher ivvut baaqirato, ella mishshum shetztzarik lebarek bimqom akila okel hu meat bammaqom hashsheni kede lebarek aach"k birkat hammazon, veal ken lekattechilla lo yaaqor belo beraka, vaapillu deim hinnicha miqtzat chaberim en zo aqira im haya atid lachazor alehem, mikkol maqom kesheholek ligmor seuddato bebayit acher hare zeh oqer mechaburato:

Vezeh eno ella beheka shello haya bedato battechilla keshebberak hammotzi ligmor bemaqom acher deaz have qebiut seuddato mittechilla bemaqom zeh, ulekak tzarik lebarek birkat hammazon bemaqom zeh velo bemaqom acher, abal im mittechilla keshebberek hammotzi haya bedato ligmor bebayit acher muttar lebarek bemaqom acher, shehare mittechilla lo qaba bemaqom zeh kol seuddato, ukemo shennohagim holeke derakim sheokelim derek hillukam veyoshebim umebarekim bimqom siyyum akilatam vehaynu mippene shellekak nitkavvenu mittechilla shello liqboa maqom laakilatam bammaqom shebbereku bo hammotzi vehitchilu sham leekol:

Bammeh debarim amurim? kesheoqer mimmeqomo harishon vegomer seuddato bammaqom hashsheni, abal im holek lammaqom hashsheni al daat lachazor limqomo harishon ligmor seuddato en zo aqira apillu lo hinnicha miqtzat chaberim, umikkol maqom aseru chakamim laasot ken mishshum dechayeshinan shemma yishkach millachazor limqomo lebarek, velo hittiru laasot ken ella raq beheka sheholek lebayit acher veokel sham, demeachar sheokel sham az vadday lo yishkach habberaka vela shekicha sheyyaqum veyelek ledarko belo beraka kelal, ulekak amerinan vadday kesheyyaqum achar akila mibbayit hashsheni yachazor limqomo harishon kede lebarek, umikkol maqom tob sheggam bikhay gavna yizzaher lekattechilla lehannicha echad al hashshulchan bammaqom harishon kaasher holek mishsham lammaqom hashsheni, vaapillu im lo nizdammen lo adam sheyyokal immo sham yannicha adam acher "p shello akal immo sham:

Vekol zeh keshehu holek lidbar hareshut, o apillu lidbar mitzva ak hi mitzva sheenah oberet, abal letzorek mitzva oberet kegon mitzvat levaya vekayyotze, o lebet hakkeneset lehitpallel im hatztzibbur "g deamerinan im bemaqom sheholek bo eno okel deaseru chaza"l laasot ken shemma yishkach millebarek legamre, im kol zeh kevan shehu tzorek mitzva oberet muttar lo lekattechilla lelek lemaqom acher laasot hammitzva ulebarek birkat hammazon kesheyyachazor limqomo, veappayv lo hinnicha miqtzat chaberim al hashshulchan, mippene sheen lehannicha mitzva oberet mishshum chashash shemma yishkach veayyen beshulchan aruk lehaggaon rabbenu zalman za"l ushear acharonim.

clarification.explanation: Just as a wandering mind during eating can require reciting the blessing again, so too a change of place may require reciting the blessing again; and since there is much dispute about this, the halachah (a doubt concerning blessings is resolved leniently) rules: one who dined in one place and recited Hamotzi, and in the midst of his meal moved to another place (even to another house, even without leaving anyone at the table) — if he let his mind wander from eating, he must recite a blessing over items that are not part of the main meal (such as fruit), if he wishes to eat them, whether in the new place or when he returns to the first place; but over items that are part of the main meal (meat, bread, and the like) he need not bless again, since his going was not considered "completion of the meal" (he still must return to his place to recite Birkat Hamazon). At the outset, one should not depart from the meal and finish it elsewhere before reciting Birkat Hamazon, unless from the very start, when he recited Hamotzi, he already intended to finish elsewhere (as is the way of travelers). And one who goes to another place intending to return — this is not a departure; nevertheless the Sages forbade doing so lest he forget to return and bless, and they permitted it only when he eats in the second place, and even then it is good to leave one person at the table, even someone who did not eat with him. An exception: when the going is for the sake of a time-bound mitzvah that cannot be postponed, such as accompanying the dead (the mitzvah of levayah) or praying with the congregation in the synagogue — it is permitted at the outset to go to the second place for the sake of fulfilling the mitzvah and to recite Birkat Hamazon only when he returns to his place, even without leaving anyone at the table; since one should not delay a time-bound mitzvah out of concern that he might forget to bless.
takeaways: Changing place in the middle of a meal: for the items of the meal itself (bread and its accompaniments) there is no new blessing; for additions (such as fruit) there is, if his mind wandered.

At the outset one should not depart from the place of the meal before Birkat Hamazon, unless this was his intention from the start (like travelers); and one who leaves intending to return should not do so unless he eats in the second place, and it is good to leave one person at the table.

For the sake of a time-bound mitzvah that cannot be postponed (such as accompanying the dead, or praying with the congregation) — it is permitted at the outset to leave the meal without leaving anyone at the table, and to recite Birkat Hamazon only upon returning.

paragraphs: Mine mezonot shebbirkatan haacharona hi meen shalosh, veken perot shel shibat hamminim veken yayin, debirkatan gam ken meen shalosh, dinam kepat leinyan aqirat maqom deasur laaqor mimmeqomo ad sheyyebarek beraka acharona, mishshum deyesh omerim kemo shehappat tzarik beraka bimqomo ken ellu tzerikin beraka acharona bimqoman, lepikak leinyan shinnuy maqom azelinan lequlla bispeq berakot veammarnin dinam kemo sheamarnu leel gabbe pat, vehu deim amad mimmeqomo harishon vehalak lechatzer acheret en amidato nechshebet gemar seuddato "p shehissicha dato milleekol, mippene shetztzarik lachazor limqomo lebarek beraka acharona velaken keshechozer veokel veshoteh apillu bemaqom acher al daat seuddato harishona hu oseh lesayyem seuddato, vekol shekken im chozer limqomo harishon veokel sheen tzarik lebarek beraka rishona, apillu lo hinnicha miqtzat chaberim:

clarification.explanation: Foods whose after-blessing is "Me'ein Shalosh" (cake and the like), and likewise fruits of the seven species, and likewise wine — their law regarding change of place is like that of bread: if he got up from his place and went to another courtyard, this is not considered the completion of his meal (he must return and recite the after-blessing in the original place), and therefore when he returns and eats or drinks them — even in another place — he does not bless again, and certainly not if he returns to his first place.
takeaways: Foods with the Me'ein Shalosh after-blessing, fruits of the seven species, and wine — their law regarding a change of place is like that of bread; they do not require a new blessing.

paragraphs: Okelin umashqin shebbirkatam haacharona hi bore nepashot rabbot, ellu lekulle alema en tzarik lebarek beraka acharona bimqom haakila o hashshetiyya, ella rashshay laamod mimmeqomo qodem beraka acharona vibarek habberaka acharona bemaqom acher, lepikak amidato mimmeqomo lelek zehu gemar seuddato, ukeshechozer veokel bammaqom hashsheni tzarik lebarek beraka rishona, v"g dela berak adayin beraka acharona al akila demaqom harishon, vaapillu shehaya bedato bammaqom harishon laleket lammaqom hashsheni veleekol sham im kol zeh meachar deshinna meqomo mibbayit zeh lebayit acher tzarik lebarek al mah sheokel babbayit hashsheni, veken name im achar shehalak labbayit hashsheni chazar limqomo harishon veakal tzarik lebarek al mah sheokel: vekol zeh im shinnuy hammaqom haya mibbayit lebayit, abal im haya mecheder lecheder bebayit echad im haya bedato meiqqara leekol bacheder hashsheni en tzarik lachazor ulebarek, veim lo haya bedato meiqqara leekol bacheder hashsheni ella aach"k nimlak vehalak lacheder hashsheni veakal tzarik lachazor ulebarek:

Vaapillu lo haya dato leekol meiqqara bacheder hashsheni im roeh maqom harishon eno chozer umebarek, vekol shekken becheder echad mippinna lepinna deeno chozer umebarek apillu lo haya dato meiqqara al zot, deha haka have tarte letebuta shehem cheder echad vegam roeh et meqomo harishon, mihu yesh choleqim bazeh usebira lehu dachashib shinnuy apillu mippinna lepinna im lo haya dato lekak vekol shekken im en roeh maqom harishon, laken lekattechilla yizzaher shello leshannot kelal, vetzarik lehazhir hamon haam bekol zot ki dabar zeh matzuy ushekicha etzel bene adam sheqqamim betok hasseuda meal hashshulchan haqqabua lahem becheder echad, veniknasim lecheder acher bishbil ezeh eseq umotzein sham perot veokelim belo beraka dechoshebim sheppeturim hem meachar shekkebar bereku al happerot shebbashshulchan ubeemet zeh have mecheder lecheder, daapillu haya bedatam meiqqara al kak kol sheen roin meqomam harishon tzarik lebarek vekol shekken heka dela haya meiqqara datam al kak:

clarification.explanation: Foods and drinks whose after-blessing is "Borei Nefashot Rabbot" — according to everyone, their after-blessing need not be recited in the place of eating, and one may get up and bless elsewhere. Therefore, his getting up from his place is considered the completion of his meal with regard to them: when he returns and eats in a new place, he must recite an opening blessing — even if he intended in advance to move there, and even if he later returns to his first place. This is when the move was from house to house; but from room to room within the same house — if he had intended from the outset to eat in the second room, he need not bless again; and if he reconsidered without prior intention, he must bless. And even without prior intention, if he can see his first place from the second room, he does not go back and bless (and all the more so from corner to corner within the same room).
takeaways: Foods whose after-blessing is "Borei Nefashot Rabbot" — moving from house to house requires a new opening blessing.
Moving from room to room: if he intended this in advance, or he can see his first place, he does not bless again.

paragraphs: "p shekkatabnu leel kol dabar shebberaka acharona shello hi meen shalosh vedino kepat hen leinyan lebarek bammaqom sheqqaba leekol, hen leinyan shinnuy maqom vekannizkar leel, haynu davqa kesheokel kazzayit shennitchayyeb bibraka acharona, abal im lo akal kazzayit dinam have kidbarim shebberaka acharona shellahem "bore nepashot rabbot" deen teunim beraka acharona bimqoman, vaapillu beokel mehem kazzayit im mittechilla lo kivven liqboa maqom laakilato ella shehaya ochez otam beyado veokel veholek, kederek bene adam sheddarkam lipamim laqachat pat habbaa bekisanin o shear perot beyadam veokelim derek hillukam betok habbayit mecheder lecheder en bazeh din shinnuy maqom vahare zeh mebarek beraka acharona bimqom siyyum akilato, deha apillu bepat ken nohagim holeke derakim leekol bederek hillukam umebarekim bimqom siyyum akilatam veen bazeh chashash ukemo shekkatabti leel:

clarification.explanation: The previous ruling (that foods with the Me'ein Shalosh after-blessing have the law of bread regarding change of place) applies only when one ate a kezayit and has already become obligated in the after-blessing; but if he did not eat a kezayit, their law is like that of items whose after-blessing is "Borei Nefashot Rabbot" (not requiring a blessing in their place). Likewise, even if he ate a kezayit, if from the outset he did not fix a place for his eating but held the fruit in his hand and ate while walking from room to room (as people are accustomed to take fruit and eat it while walking) — this is not considered a change of place, and he recites the after-blessing in the place where he finishes eating.
takeaways: Eating less than a kezayit, or eating while walking without fixing a place — these do not carry the law of change of place.

paragraphs: Mi sheakal pat o shear debarim debirkatan meen shalosh deamarnu sheeno rashshay lekattechilla lelek ligmor seuddato bemaqom acher qodem sheyyebarek beraka acharona, hinneh im abar al daat chakamim veyatza mimmeqomo velo berek, ben im yatza bemezid ben beshogeg yachazor limqomo vibarek, im en hammaqom rachoq kol kak sheyyesh chashash dead sheyyachazor yitakkel hammazon bemeayv, v"g dekatebu happoseqim za"l taqqana lazeh sheyyokal kazzayit pat bammaqom hashsheni vibarek sham, en taqqana zo berura lepum dati yaan ki yikkanes bazeh besapeq bebirkat hammotzi, mihu yesh taqqana acheret muskemet allibba dekulle alema sheyyihyeh adam acher okel kazzayit pat vibarek alayv hammotzi vikavven liptor et zeh, veim i epshar lo bekak tzarik lachazor limqomo vibarek:

Bammeh debarim amurim? beheka deepshar lo lachazor, abal im holek badderek veen mamtinin lo, hinneh zeh apillu yatza bemezid en tzarik lachazor meqomo, shehare bediabad im berek bammaqom shennizkar qayma lan deyatza bekol gavna usheat haddechaq kediabad dame, veken name im maqom harishon sheakal bo eno naqi vei epshar lo lenaqqoto atta, yakol lelek lachutz ulebarek "g deeno okel bammaqom hashsheni, vegam bazeh shehu yotze mimmaqom zeh lammaqom hashsheni mechamat hanneqiyyut im yizdammen lo bammaqom hashsheni adam sheyyokal vibarek vikavven alayv hinneh mah tob umah naim, veayyen chesed laalapim qp"d seip qatan ':

clarification.explanation: One who ate bread or an item whose blessing is Me'ein Shalosh, and transgressed the ruling and left his place before reciting the after-blessing (deliberately or inadvertently) — should return to his place and bless, provided the place is not too far (lest the food be digested). One should not rely on the remedy of eating a kezayit of bread in the new place and blessing there (since that itself introduces a doubt concerning the blessing of Hamotzi); rather, the agreed-upon remedy is that another person eat a kezayit of bread and recite Hamotzi with the intent to exempt him. If this is not possible, he must return to his place. But if he is on the road and cannot return, or if the first place is unclean, he may bless in the place where he finds himself (a case of pressing need is treated like after the fact).
takeaways: Left his place without reciting the after-blessing — he returns to bless, or has another person recite Hamotzi and exempt him.
Unable to return (on the road, or an unclean place) — he blesses in the place where he finds himself.

paragraphs: Apillu mechamat sibba qetanna muttar laqum mikkan lekan bemaqom echad betok d' ammot ulebarek, yaan dekol arba ammot chashubim maqom echad bekamma debarim abal chutz learba ammot en lebarek bishbil sibba qetanna ella davqa besibba gedola vehekreach rab hammakricho al kak, veayyen chayye adam kelal m"z ot va"v vehannizhar gam tok d' ammot tabo alayv beraka:

clarification.explanation: Even for a minor reason, one is permitted to get up and move within four amot in the same place and bless there, since four amot are considered a single place for many purposes; but beyond four amot, one should not bless from there on account of a minor reason, but only for a major reason and a genuine necessity.
takeaways: A change of place within four amot is not considered a change of place at all — one may bless there for any reason.

paragraphs: Hannitzrak linqabayv betok seuddato en zeh chashib hepseq, veen tzarik lebarek keshechozer veokel, vegam beraka shel netilat yadayim en tzarik lebarek mishshum deyesh pelugta bazeh vesapeq berakot lehaqel, veraq yeharher birkat al netilat yadayim belibbo:

clarification.explanation: One who goes out to relieve himself (to the bathroom) in the middle of his meal — this is not considered an interruption, and he need not bless again when he returns and eats. And he need not recite the blessing on washing the hands again either (due to the dispute — a doubt concerning blessings is resolved leniently), but should merely contemplate the blessing in his heart.
takeaways: Leaving to relieve oneself in the middle of a meal is not an interruption; and one need not bless again on washing the hands (only contemplate it).

paragraphs: Im hipsiq betok seuddato lehitpallel ap al gab dela chashib hepseq leinyan beraka, mikkol maqom yittol yadayv belo beraka dintilat yadayim, mishshum deikka pelugta bazeh veim en lo mayim yismok al hammeqillin:

clarification.explanation: One who interrupted his meal in order to pray — even though this is not considered an interruption with regard to Birkat Hamazon — should nonetheless wash his hands without a blessing (due to the dispute); and if he has no water, he may rely on those who are lenient.
takeaways: Interrupting the meal to pray — one washes the hands without a blessing upon returning.

paragraphs: Im akal perot began echad vehalak legan acher tzarik lachazor ulebarek apillu im hem semukim, vaapillu im keshebberak techilla haya dato al zeh, vehu haddin began echad im lo haya dato mittechilla al hakkol, tzarik lebarek al kol ilan veilan hannimlak leekol mimmennu, vaapillu akal bemizrachah shel teena uba leekol bemaarabah tzarik lachazor ulebarek im lo haya dato mittechilla lekak, velav davqa mipperot haggan ella kol sheokel sham debarim sheenan tzerikin beraka bimqoman dina haki:

Beme debarim amurim? keshehaggan muqqap mechitztzot, abal im eno muqqap mechitztzot en dato moelet lekol hailanot ella haddabar taluy beroeh et meqomo harishon, sheim bammaqom hashsheni roeh meqomo harishon eno mebarek, veim eno roeh hen mechamat richuq hen mechamat ezeh hepseq sheyyesh benehem hare zeh mebarek, ubesipri haq' mqbtzyl chaqarti bs"d im eno roeh kol meqomo ella miqtzato may, veim tirtzeh lomar roeh miqtzato saggi vela baenan kullo, hinneh im roehu keshehu omed veeno roehu keshehu yosheb may, veheka deomed veokel la qamibbaya lan, ak mibbaya lan keshehu yosheb veokel veeno roehu, i amerinan kevan deim yaamod roehu mehanne, o dilma la mehanne. veim timtze lomar kevan deim amad haya roehu mehanne, hinneh im haya omed betok gumma veeno roehu, abal im haya omed al sepat haggumma roehu may, vesham hebeti bs"d mah shekkatabti baggemara dizbachim dap qy"ch kol sepeqot ellu gabbe akilat qadashim birayat shiloh, vesapeq harishon nipshat mishsham dimhanne reiyya shel miqtzato ki ken peshita leh lerab pappa sham, umah shekkatub babbarayta tana roeh sheameru roeh kullo veku' en haggirsa haamittit ken ukemo shekkatab "tzon qadashim" ushear sepeqot deniddon didan hem beayot derab pappa verabbi yirmeya sham denisharu betequ, veayyen mah shekkatab b"chq natan" za"l bekavvana d"m timtza lomar" deqaamar hatam, veyadua deikka pelugta b"m timtza lomar" im peshituta hi im lav, velaken kevan dehashsha"s massiq hatam betequ ken sepeqot deniddon didan nisharu besapeq velo yebarek, ketzad yaaseh mebi adam acher sheyyebarek vikavven lepatero veaz yokal, vesham besipri haq' mqbtzyl katabti dispeqot ellu kullam shayyakim bedin hammegilla besiman trtz"ch gabbe kerakkim hammuqqapim choma dikparim hannirin immahem qorin kemotam ayyen sham, vesham hebeti mah sheyyesh lehaqshot miggemara dimgilla dap g' ammud b' beshinnuy dimshanne rabbi yirmeya kegon sheyyashabta benachal veku', veal baaya derabbi yirmeya atzmo debae baggemara dizbachim hannizkeret, veshub asiti chilluq nakon ben ha dimgilla lehatam dizbachim hannizkeret, veassiqena al kol panim niddon didan gabbe berakot shel happerot dame lahem mammash leha dizbachim:

clarification.explanation:
One who ate fruit in one garden and moved to another garden must bless again, even if the gardens are adjacent and even if when he first blessed he had already intended to eat in the second garden as well. And the same applies within the very same garden: if he had not intended from the outset to eat from all the trees, he must bless anew on each tree he reconsiders and decides to eat from — and even if he ate on the eastern side of a fig tree and comes to eat on its western side, he must go back and bless if he had not intended this in advance. This law is not specific to garden fruit, but applies to any place where one eats items that do not require a new blessing, as long as one remains within that same "place."
When does this ruling (that an intention from the start of the meal exempts the whole garden) apply? When the garden is enclosed by partitions. But if the garden is not enclosed by partitions, the initial intention does not suffice for all the trees; rather, everything depends on whether, from the new place, he can still see his first place: if he can see it, he does not bless again; if he cannot see it (whether on account of distance or on account of some partition between them), he blesses anew.
The Ben Ish Chai adds that in his book Mikabtzi'el he raised several practical doubts on this matter: What is the law if he sees only part of his first place and not all of it — is this sufficient? And what is the law if he sees his place while standing, but does not see it while sitting? And what is the law if he was standing inside a pit and cannot see from there, as opposed to standing at the edge of the pit, from where he can see it? He discusses these questions by comparing them to similar doubts raised by the Sages in the Talmud (in Zevachim, and in the laws of the Megillah regarding walled cities), some of which remained there unresolved ("teiku"). His practical conclusion: since these doubts remain without a clear resolution, one should not bless out of doubt. The practical solution is to bring another person who will bless with the intent to exempt him, and only then to eat.
takeaways: Ate in one garden and moved to an adjacent garden — a new blessing is required, even if he intended in advance to eat in both.
In a garden enclosed by partitions, an intention from the start of eating exempts all the trees in it; in a garden not enclosed by partitions, it depends on whether he can see his previous place.

When there is doubt as to whether he can see his previous place (for example, he sees it standing but not sitting, or he stood inside a pit and did not see from there) — it is best not to bless himself, but to bring another person who will bless and exempt him. (Seeing only part of his previous place is considered sufficient and does not require a new blessing.)

paragraphs: Gamar seuddato venatal yadayv mayim acharonim, veken hu haddin im amar hab lan unebarek "p shello natal yadayv adayin, hare zeh eno yakol leekol velishtot ad sheyyebarek birkat hammazon veap al pi sheyyesh bekol zeh pelugta vekamma chilluqe deot hinneh zeh hu haiqqar ledina mishshum sapeq berakot, sheim lo natal yadayv velo amar hab lan unebarek ella raq gamar belibbo shello leekol, o shessilleq et hashshulchan o sheamar tenu venittol yadenu velo amar unebarek, az lekulle alema muttar leekol debarim hatztzerikim beraka lipnehem kegon lehabi perot o mashqin shello berek adayin alehem betok hasseuda ulebarek alehem, abal debarim shebberek kebar alehem betok hasseuda lo yokal mippene hassapeq shel habberaka deikka bazeh pelugta velo yaknis atzmo beyadayim bispeq berakot, vekol zeh kesheggamar bedato shello leekol, abal im amar hab lan unebarek vehaya bedato lihyot okel ad sheyyabiu lo mayim littol yadayv hare zeh muttar leekol lekulle alema velo yebarek veayyen chesed laalapim, umi shessomek al shulchan acherim apillu amar hab lan unebarek la have hessach haddaat im lo ratza baal habbayit, demissetama dato taluy birtzon baal habbayit, mihu im beet sheamar ken hissicha dato beberur sheggamar bedato sheapillu baal habbayit lo yirtzeh bekak vibaqqesh mimmennu leekol velishtot od hu yaaseh lo hitnatztzelut velo yokal veyishteh, hare zeh chashib hessach haddaat, veim amar baal habbayit hab lan unebarek veshatequ vehiskimu kullam lidbarayv chashib hessach haddaat lekullam, abal im echad mehem lo hiskim lidbarayv vehaya bedato leekol od lo chashib hessach haddaat lezeh haadam veyukal leekol velishtot:

clarification.explanation:
One who finished his meal and washed with Mayim Acharonim, and likewise one who said "Hav lan u'nevareich" (even though he has not yet washed) — can no longer eat or drink until he recites Birkat Hamazon. And although there are several differing opinions about all this, this is the essential ruling in practice, on account of the doubt concerning blessings.
But if he did not wash and did not say "Hav lan u'nevareich," but merely decided in his heart not to eat anymore, or cleared the table, or said "give us [water] and let us wash" without "and let us bless" — then according to everyone he is permitted to eat items that require a blessing before them (such as fruit or drinks he had not yet blessed during the meal), and to bless over them; but items he already blessed during the meal, he should not eat, on account of the doubt, so as not to knowingly enter into a doubt concerning blessings.
All this is when he decided in his mind not to eat anymore; but if he said "Hav lan u'nevareich" while intending to continue eating until they bring him water to wash — he is permitted to eat according to everyone, and need not bless again.
And one who relies on another's table (a guest) — even if he said "Hav lan u'nevareich," this is not a wandering of the mind, since his mind is dependent on the will of the host — unless he clearly decided in his heart not to eat anymore, even if the host asks him to. And if the host said "Hav lan u'nevareich" and everyone remained silent and agreed — this is a wandering of the mind for all of them; but one who did not agree and intended to eat more, it is not a wandering of the mind for him, and he may eat and drink.
takeaways: Mayim Acharonim, or "Hav lan u'nevareich" — one may not eat or drink until Birkat Hamazon (on account of the doubt concerning blessings).
Deciding in his heart alone, or merely clearing the table — permits eating new items with a blessing, but not items already blessed.
A guest — "Hav lan u'nevareich" is not a wandering of the mind unless he firmly decided so; silent agreement by all present is a wandering of the mind for all of them.

paragraphs: Im minhag hammedina kesheyyesh chabura okelim veshotim uba echad mibbachutz veniknas etzlam shemmoshitin lo kol echad kos, lo yebarek ella al kos rishon demissetama keshebberak dato al kol mah sheyyittenu lo, umihu tob lekavven beperush mittechilla kesheyyebarek liptor kol kosot sheyyittenu lo achar kak:

clarification.explanation: If it is the local custom that when a person joins a group that is drinking from outside, they hand him cups one after another — he blesses only over the first cup, since his mind was generally on everything they would give him; nevertheless, it is good to intend explicitly in advance, in his first blessing, to exempt all the cups to come.
takeaways: One who joins a group drinking cups blesses only over the first one (an explicit prior intention is preferable).
